userMessage:
I think that would be good. We also want to follow this template in the future: https://www.notion.so/acme/Weekly-update-template-2a7c9e1b4d6f48a0b3c5d7e9f1a2b4c6

So generally, I'd say we're interested in: what goes well, what doesn't, high-level of what happened, what's planned next week, release time/version

messages.text: The weekly updates this workflow writes are too verbose. Make the summary shorter and easier to read for people outside the team.

I rewrote the summary instructions so the output is a short status brief: At a glance, Going well, Needs attention, Upcoming releases. A test run on last week's Linear updates worked. The change is saved as a draft. One thing I noticed: the brief dropped the release version for one project. If release versions matter to your readers, I can tell it to always keep them. Should I do that?

workflows.name: Weekly Linear Project Updates Summary to Notion

rationale: Mid-edit, the user links a Notion page. Notion is connected, and the open workflow has a Notion credential: the agent must read the page with the Notion MCP tools, not with an HTTP Request through execute_node.
